scope: Incremental SQL revision 4 policy, abstract proof model and preserved revision 3 backup failure; approval does not assert completed implementation or backup recovery.
findings: Revision 3 full pg_dump failed at native SQL PREPARE after 68 admitted queries; its evidence remains preserved, not counted as successful recovery.

Native PREPARE stores the exact admitted source including a nonempty body span into the same abstract statement table as protocol Parse. SQL EXECUTE requires its own admitted request and lookup of a known statement; reachable-state induction proves the target is admitted.

The abstract SQL-prepared statement can be bound to a protocol portal; cache lookup leaves statement state unchanged; a missing name denies native execution. Witnesses cover native PREPARE and EXECUTE.
Revision 4 requires sole top-level statements, conservative ASCII name handling, nested opaque/mode checks and full unmodified pg_dump/restore tests. These remain implementation and test obligations.
limitations: Lean assumes request classification, source/body span, exact byte interpretation, binary/profile pinning and truthful parser reports; bodyPart is a nonempty substring condition and does not independently establish an Alloy or PostgreSQL grammar derivation.

The model does not prove SQL name normalization, trusted parser production classification, atomic protocol processing, backend acceptance, cross-protocol wire correspondence, prepared object lifetimes, resource limits or implementation refinement.
Optimistic provenance may survive backend errors; server execution failure is not success. The revision 3 backup failure stays BLOCKED until real full backup and restore pass through the proxy.
Six reviews and the final frozen-input two-clean-build gate against the revision 3 production snapshot are required before production changes.
